summary: Documents object identifiers assigned in the arc donated by RSA Data Security to the S/MIME working group, transfers it to IANA, and sets allocation policies. This is administrative bookkeeping rather than a protocol.

eli5.summary: A list of numbered tags one group received, with new rules for handing out more.

questions: what is the s/mime object identifier arc
subtitle: Who holds the S/MIME object identifier arc, what is already numbered inside it, and how new numbers get handed out.

tldr.problem: RSA Data Security donated an object identifier arc to the S/MIME Mail Security Working Group, and the working group's assignments in it needed to be written down and given a permanent home.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC lists the thirteen subordinate arcs that were used, hands control of the arc to IANA, and asks IANA to create registry tables with a Specification Required plus Expert Review policy for future entries.
tldr.outcome: The S/MIME arc is now an IANA-managed registry, with new values limited to work strongly related to S/MIME and CMS.

today: RFC 7107 is an Informational RFC. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it, and the text transfers control of the arc to IANA.

sections.title: The Donated S/MIME Arc
sections.content:
When the S/MIME Mail Security Working Group was chartered, RSA Data Security donated an object identifier arc for its use. Object identifiers are primarily used with Abstract Syntax Notation One (ASN.1), and they work with any and all versions of ASN.1.

The arc is id-smime, defined as { iso(1) member-body(2) us(840) rsadsi(113549) pkcs(1) pkcs9(9) 16 }. The RFC does three things: it describes the identifiers that were assigned in the arc, it transfers control of the arc to IANA, and it sets IANA allocation policies for future assignments.
sections.eli5: A company gave a group a long block of special numbers. This paper explains what the group already used and who is in charge from now on.

sections.title: The Thirteen Subordinate Arcs
sections.content:
Thirteen subordinate arcs were used, numbered from zero to twelve. Each one groups a kind of identifier: id-mod (0) for ASN.1 modules, id-ct (1) for Cryptographic Message Syntax (CMS) content types, id-aa (2) for attributes, id-alg (3) for algorithm identifiers, and so on up to id-pskc (12) for Portable Symmetric Key Container (PSKC) attributes.

The other arcs cover certificate distribution (4), signature policy qualifiers (5), commitment type identifiers (6), test security policies (7), symmetric key distribution control attributes (8), signature type identifiers (9), encoded information types (10) and S/MIME capabilities (11).
sections.eli5: The big block was split into thirteen smaller drawers, and each drawer holds one kind of label, such as one for algorithms and one for attributes.

sections.title: What IANA Is Asked to Create
sections.content:
IANA is asked to update one registry table and create fourteen additional tables. The update adds the entry 1.2.840.113549.1.9.16, named smime, to the "SMI Security for Mechanism Codes" registry, because that registry normally holds positive integers and the donated value cannot be described that way.

Each new table lists decimal values, a description and a reference. For example, the module identifier table includes id-mod-cms pointing at RFC 2630, and the content type table includes id-ct-receipt pointing at RFC 2634. Some entries are marked "Reserved and Obsolete".
sections.eli5: The office keeps a notebook page for every drawer. Each line says what the number means and which document explains it, and some lines say the number is retired.

sections.title: Rules for Future Assignments
sections.content:
Updates to the new tables require both Specification Required and Expert Review, as defined in RFC 5226. The expert is expected to ensure that any new values are strongly related to the work done by the S/MIME Mail Security Working Group.

Examples the RFC gives are content types, attributes, and identifiers for algorithms used with S/MIME and CMS. Object identifiers for other purposes should not be assigned in this arc.
sections.eli5: To get a new number you need a written explanation and an expert who agrees it fits. Numbers for unrelated things belong somewhere else.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC states that it populates an IANA registry and raises no new security considerations. The protocols that specify these values carry the security considerations that go with their usage.
sections.eli5: This is just a list of labels, so it does not add new dangers. The documents that use the labels explain their own safety rules.
